meaning: A person who sat at a big board of sockets and cords. They connected phone calls by hand, plugging one line into another.
clues: It helped people make phone calls.
It was a job done by a person, not a machine.
The person would answer with "Number, please?" when you lifted the phone.
They plugged cords into holes on a big board to link each call by hand.
It has two words. The first has eleven letters and starts with S.
assumes: A payphone is a public phone
A phone book lists names and numbers

decoys.meaning: A public phone that you used by putting in coins or using a card.
A thick book listing the names, addresses, and phone numbers of people in an area.
A machine that answers the phone when you are away and records a message from the caller.

exchange.speaker: floyd
exchange.text: Back in my day, you lifted the phone and a friendly voice said "Number, please?" Then they plugged you through.

exchange.speaker: bud
exchange.text: Today's version: your phone connects calls by itself in a blink. Just tap a name in your contacts.

exchange.speaker: floyd
exchange.text: No cords, no waiting. I do miss those friendly voices, though.
